questions.q: In a MongoDB replica set, which member accepts writes?
options: All members accept writes simultaneously
Any secondary, at any time
Only the primary
Only the arbiter
questions.explain: Exactly one member, the primary, accepts writes at any given moment; secondaries replicate from it.

questions.q: What is the oplog, and why is it described as a genuine analog to a SQL Server transaction log?
options: A backup file created once per day
A log of failed queries only, unrelated to replication
A capped collection recording every write on the primary in order, which secondaries tail and replay — both are ordered, replayable records of change, not just similarly named
A configuration file listing replica set members
questions.explain: The oplog is what replication actually is in MongoDB — secondaries replay it to stay current, just as a transaction log drives log shipping.

questions.q: What happens to a secondary that falls behind and drops outside the oplog's capped window?
options: It requires a full resync
Nothing — it catches up instantly regardless of how far behind it is
The primary shuts down
It automatically becomes the new primary
questions.explain: Once a secondary is too far behind for the capped oplog to cover the gap, replaying is no longer possible and a full resync is needed.

questions.q: What role does an arbiter play in a replica set?
options: It replaces the need for an oplog
It holds a full copy of the data and can become primary
It votes in elections but holds no data itself
It performs backups automatically
questions.explain: An arbiter exists purely to vote, useful for keeping the voting member count odd without the cost of an extra data-bearing node.

questions.q: What is the real tradeoff during a replica set election, per this lesson?
options: All secondaries are permanently promoted to primary
The oplog is deleted during every election
There is briefly no primary, and writes that hadn't yet replicated to the newly elected primary can be rolled back
There is no tradeoff — failover is instantaneous and lossless
questions.explain: The lesson names this honestly: during the election window the set can't accept writes, and unreplicated data can be lost via rollback.
